topStory.headline: Penn State Western Campuses Develop Distinct A.I. Literacy Approaches
topStory.summary:
Penn State's three western campuses — Beaver, Behrend, and Greater Allegheny — are taking different approaches to A.I. literacy while sharing a focus on thoughtful engagement with tools, according to Penn State University. At Beaver, Ashu Kumar embeds A.I. lessons into every course, emphasizing that effective prompting requires skill. At Behrend, Kyle Chalupczynski discovered students were not questioning A.I. outputs, leading him to grade their engagement with chatbots rather than just their use of them.

At Greater Allegheny, faculty are encountering students who "don't want it to replace their learning" but value human connection. Behrend created literacy profiles for staff, faculty, and students, then worked backward to determine what support was needed. Greater Allegheny sponsors monthly "A.I. du Jour" workshops bringing different campus constituencies together.

Kumar's approach included having a student intern meet individually with staff to suggest A.I. implementations for their workflows. Chalupczynski's grading rubric for A.I. engagement requires more assessment work for faculty. The campuses discovered their approaches through experimentation rather than comprehensive planning.

stories.headline: Modesto Junior College Students Call for Clearer A.I. Standards
stories.summary: Modesto Junior College is working to establish clearer guidelines for A.I. usage as students navigate evolving academic policies, according to ABC10. The institution is part of broader efforts among community colleges to develop consistent standards for artificial intelligence in coursework.

stories.headline: Chronicle Plans Virtual Forum on A.I. Agents in Campus Operations
stories.summary: The Chronicle of Higher Education will host a virtual forum April 9 exploring how A.I. agents could automate administrative tasks like financial aid and facilities management, according to The Chronicle. The event will address data security safeguards and staff concerns about A.I.'s impact on their roles.

stories.headline: Bucks County School Districts Adopt Varied A.I. Policies
stories.summary: Bucks County school districts are implementing different approaches to generative A.I., from pilot programs using Microsoft Copilot to formal policies with assignment scales, according to BUCKSCO.Today. Some districts have created A.I. think tanks while others participate in University of Pennsylvania literacy programs.

stories.headline: A.I. Detection Tools Adapt to Student Usage Patterns
stories.summary: Copyleaks reports that 90% of students now use A.I. in academic work, with 53% using it weekly, according to Copyleaks. The company is developing new detection features for hybrid human-A.I. content, custom models, and multimodal assignments as paraphrasing tools become more sophisticated.

stories.headline: Free A.I. Detection Tool Sees Increased Student Adoption
stories.summary: Detector.io is seeing increased use among students who want to check their own work before submission, according to Morocco World News. The free tool analyzes up to 3,000 words for A.I.-generated patterns, reflecting a shift toward students self-monitoring their writing processes.

stories.headline: Lucknow University Flags Plagiarism in 95% of PhD Theses
stories.summary: Lucknow University detected plagiarism in 95% of PhD theses submitted this year, according to MSN. The finding underscores ongoing academic integrity challenges alongside emerging A.I. content concerns.
